nodes.label: analytics aggregate tables (analytics_daily/_page_views/_referrers/_visitors)
nodes.rationale: No IP or user-agent is stored; the visitor hash salt rotates daily, so a visitor is recognizable only within one day — 'visitors' over a range is the sum of daily values, not a distinct-person count.

nodes.label: CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: P3-4: previously npm run build on deploy was the only check, catching type errors too late; this workflow runs on every push/PR to block earlier.

nodes.label: docker-socket-proxy service
nodes.rationale: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy filters only path+method, not the request body — POST+CONTAINERS is root-equivalent by itself. The effective boundary is network isolation (docker-proxy-net, internal:true), not the API-group flags.

nodes.label: provisioning-agent service
nodes.rationale: mem_limit set after finding an unbounded nixpacks build (1-2GB) could push the kernel OOM-killer to pick PostgreSQL by oom_score, taking the DB of every tenant offline.

nodes.label: tenant api (PostgREST) service
nodes.rationale: PGRST_DB_PREPARED_STATEMENTS disabled because PgBouncer runs transaction pool mode, where prepared statements are session state and break across pooled connections, causing sporadic 500s under load.

nodes.label: tenant auth (GoTrue) service
nodes.rationale: GOTRUE_API_PORT set explicitly because the healthcheck must hit the same port; previously left implicit, it didn't match the healthcheck port and containers reported unhealthy despite working.

nodes.label: GitHub webhook deploy routing
nodes.rationale: The webhook router is mounted under prefix '/webhooks' with an inner route named '/github/:projectId'; an earlier version put the full path in the inner route too, so the effective endpoint was /webhooks/webhooks/... and GitHub always got 401 — a push never triggered a deployment.

nodes.label: P0-1: Docker socket proxy network isolation
nodes.norm_label: p0-1: docker socket proxy network isolation
nodes.rationale: Before: docker-socket-proxy was reachable from every customer container with no auth — POST /containers/create with a root bind mount and privileged:true gave root on the host. Fix: moved the proxy off traefik-net into an internal-only docker-proxy-net that only the agent joins.

nodes.label: PgBouncer AUTH_QUERY against pgbouncer_auth
nodes.rationale: The pgbouncer image only generates userlist.txt from DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD (just 'postgres'), so per-tenant authenticator_<slug> roles aren't in it. AUTH_QUERY authenticates them directly against pg_shadow instead of silently mapping them to postgres, which would make PostgREST superuser in every tenant DB and bypass RLS everywhere. AUTH_DBNAME=postgres is required because the auth function only exists in the 'postgres' database — without it every tenant DB's AUTH_QUERY fails and GoTrue/PostgREST can never connect.

nodes.label: Per-project Docker network as runtime-only state
nodes.norm_label: per-project docker network as runtime-only state
nodes.rationale: app-<slug>-net membership is created at deploy time (ensureProjectNetwork) and exists only as live Docker daemon state — it's in no docker-compose.yml. Recreating Traefik, the agent, or MinIO rebuilds their networks from the compose file and the project networks are lost, causing silent 504s. The agent re-establishes these connections for all projects on every start.

nodes.label: kunden table
nodes.rationale: db_provisioned and db_enabled kept as separate flags so the database layer is optional and switchable after creation: disabling is just docker compose down (RAM freed, data untouched, dashboard table/SQL editor keeps working via PgBouncer).

nodes.label: cms_config role (Migration 22)
nodes.rationale: Not in the original design — added because the CMS service also needs to read cms_collections/cms_users etc., and using the superuser for that would defeat the point of the restricted per-tenant roles; cms_config has rights on only the cms_* tables and explicitly enumerated kunden columns (secret columns excluded).

nodes.label: cms service
nodes.rationale: One shared service for all tenants, not one container per customer — the tenant comes from the session; a container per customer would repeat the RAM waste Migration 19 removed.

nodes.label: cms_audit table
nodes.rationale: Kept separate from audit_logs (the operator log) so the customer can be shown their own history.

nodes.label: cms_users table
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not GoTrue: GoTrue is optional per tenant (Migration 19) and can be disabled while the CMS still runs; also these are the operator's editors, not the customer's app users.

nodes.label: Postgres memory tuning for 8GB VPS
nodes.rationale: Old values (shared_buffers=1GB, max_connections=150, work_mem=32MB) were sized for a 16GB blueprint; on 8GB Postgres became the largest process and the one the kernel OOM-killer picked when a nixpacks build requested 2GB, taking the DB offline for every tenant. New values keep total memory under 1.5GB instead of up to 3GB, freeing roughly 1GB — about two more tenants of headroom.

nodes.label: Rate limiting keyed on Cf-Connecting-Ip
nodes.rationale: Learned from a load test: keying on the TCP peer failed because behind Cloudflare that peer is always one of a handful of edge IPs, spreading a limit across many buckets — 600 requests in 5s against a 20/s limit let 576 through. After switching to the Cf-Connecting-Ip header, the same test yields 463/600 as 429, matching the theoretical burst+rate value.

nodes.label: .claude/hooks/*.sh
nodes.rationale: Beenden sich still mit Exit 0, wenn graphify nicht installiert ist.

nodes.label: graphify CLI Tool
nodes.rationale: Liest das Repo deterministisch per AST aus, damit KI-Assistenten einen zugeschnittenen Teilgraphen statt Volltextsuche über 200 Dateien bekommen.

nodes.label: graphify-out/cache/semantic/
nodes.rationale: Inhaltsbasierter Cache erspart denselben LLM-Lauf erneut.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Tunnel
nodes.rationale: Admin-Zugriff ohne offenen Port.

nodes.label: CMS Session-Gültigkeitsprüfung
nodes.rationale: Prüft bei jedem Aufruf, ob das Konto noch existiert und nicht gesperrt ist — ein Cookie allein ist kein Zugang.

nodes.label: docker-socket-proxy
nodes.rationale: EXEC und VOLUMES abgeschaltet; API-Gruppen-Flags filtern nur Pfad/Methode, nicht den Request-Body — die wirksame Grenze ist die Netzwerktrennung, nicht die Flags.

nodes.label: NextAuth v5
nodes.rationale: Läuft als Beta mit Caret-Range (offener Punkt).

nodes.label: Rate-Limiting via Cf-Connecting-Ip
nodes.rationale: Traefik sah als Gegenstelle immer eine Cloudflare-Edge-IP, wodurch das Limit wirkungslos war; nach Umstellung auf Cf-Connecting-Ip liefert der Lasttest 463 von 600 Anfragen korrekt als 429.

nodes.label: Bekannte offene Punkte
nodes.rationale: Keine Testsuite vorhanden — sieben von elf schweren Audit-Befunden wären durch vier Integrationstests gefunden worden, der Cloudflare-Rate-Limit-Fund jedoch nur durch einen Lasttest gegen die echte Kette.

nodes.label: Sicherheitsaudit-Historie
nodes.rationale: Vollständiges Production-Readiness-Audit am 10.08.2026 (Commit 0430f9c); P0-Befunde in Sprint 21 behoben (Netzwerk-Isolation, Tenant-Isolation via REVOKE CONNECT + Rollen, Advisory Lock, Secret-Maskierung, wiederherstellbare Backups). Zweiter Durchgang am 18.08.2026 behob fünf weitere Befunde (Feldprüfung, Login-Rate-Limit, Upload-Fläche, Postgres-Fehlermeldungen, zeitkonstanter Secret-Vergleich).

nodes.label: SQL-Editor (Single-Admin-Werkzeug)
nodes.rationale: Bewusst als Single-Admin-Werkzeug hinter Auth + Cloudflare Zero Trust gedacht, nicht für Multi-User-Zugriff mit unterschiedlichen Rechten.

nodes.label: Upload-Härtung (EXIF-Entfernung, Größenlimits)
nodes.rationale: Dateigröße sagt nichts über den Speicher des dekodierten Bildes; ohne Grenzen für Pixelzahl/Bildanzahl kippt eine kleine Datei den gemeinsamen Container.

nodes.label: GitHub-Webhook HMAC-SHA256-Verifikation
nodes.rationale: Signatur wird in konstanter Zeit gegen den rohen Request-Body geprüft, um Timing-Angriffe zu verhindern.
